text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Egypt begins work on projects signed with Kuwait during last week's Middle East economic conference in Cairo.
- Kuwait Investment Authority to allow government institutions to take shares in privatised state holdings as of 1997.

- Investment official says futures trading on the Kuwait Stock Exchange to include currencies, goods and stocks. Kuwait last month approved futures trading on the exchange which will start at a later stage.

- Kuwait National Petroleum Company (KNPC) says workers at oil export terminal and refineries did not go on strike. KNPC's labour union on Wednesday suspended a possible strike at Mina al-Ahmadi after three hours of talks with company officials.
- Parliament to meet on Saturday to discuss pending agenda items. Tuesday's session was dominated by a dispute over the election of speaker.
- Three Kuwaitis sentenced to death for killing a countryman who allegedly sexullay assaulted a young boy.
- Parliament likely to mandate comprehensive verdict on dispute over speaker's post. MP Jassem al-Kharafi says the October 20 re-election of speaker Ahmad al-Saadoun was unconstitutional.
